scope: 64-bit Linux thread CPU clock only. Public signatures and the existing first-component time / zero second-component convention are unchanged. Other Unix, Apple and Windows paths remain unchanged and unfinished under #89.
change: Uses rustix 1.1.5 clock_gettime_dynamic with Known(ThreadCPUTime), preserving fallibility and the zero pair on error. Successful seconds and nanoseconds are cast to f64 separately and combined in the original arithmetic order.
source_evidence: Pinned rustix src/clockid.rs maps ThreadCPUTime to CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID. backend/libc/time/syscalls.rs clock_gettime_dynamic calls libc clock_gettime once on the selected non-fix_y2038 backend, returning its initialized timespec on success and an error otherwise. build.rs excludes the supported Linux x86_64 and aarch64 LP64 targets from fix_y2038. The infallible clock API was not selected because it would lose the error fallback.
dependency: Enables time on existing rustix 1.1.5 with std/fs/use-libc retained. No package version or lockfile changes. cargo deny --all-features check and cargo audit passed. Dependency unsafe remains a separate trust boundary.
fixtures: Committed conversion fixtures passed before and after replacement: missing timestamp, zero, fractional seconds and rounding at 2^53. Both components are compared by bits. These fixtures test conversion and fallback, not an injected failing native syscall.
inventory: Linux x86_64 and arm64 cpu_native.rs compiler primary spans decrease from 6 to 4. Source counts remain unchanged because the existing direct call is still compiled on other non-Apple Unix targets. macOS and Windows inventories are unchanged. Local x86_64 compiler inventory passed; native matrices remain pending.
